posture_findings: [H2005] Hip extensor moment arms peak near full extension; summed hip-extensor leverage is about 94% of peak at -15 deg hip flexion from the fully columnar pose. The authors conclude T. rex is best reconstructed 'more upright (although not completely columnar)', not crouched. Columnar poses were less effective than poses with slight flexion.

[H2005 Table 1] Model joint ranges (0 = straight column): hip flexion/extension -65 to +45 deg, abduction 0 to 45, long-axis rotation -30 to +30, knee -10 to 90, ankle -90 to 0, MTP -45 to 90, interphalangeal -45 to 0. Conversion to Hutchinson & Garcia 2002 angles: hip -90, knee 180 minus angle, ankle +180, toe +90.

[H2005 App. 2] Default limb geometry: hip abducted 10 deg to clear the trunk, tibiotarsus given 15 deg valgus so the lower leg returns medially to match footprints. Joint gaps add +7.5% femur, +5% tibiotarsus and +10% metatarsus (foot pad). Femoral head radius 0.10 m in a 0.15 m acetabulum.

[H2004, HG2002] Large theropods used fairly upright limbs; a ~6000 kg T. rex would need an unreasonably large extensor mass to run fast. [MCCREA2014] A flexed pose (knee 110 deg, ankle 140 deg, per HG2002) lowers hip height to 0.80 of straight-leg height. [GATESY2009, unverified search summary] Constraint-based exclusion leaves poses 'neither very columnar nor very flexed'.

[SELLERS2017] With realistic bone stress (~100 MPa) the Stan model is limited to walking or grounded running (Froude ~1.0). Its 7.7 m/s maximum appears only with unrealistic stress limits. The model is a 7206.7 kg BHI 3033 reconstruction with hinge joints restricted to the sagittal plane.

[SELLERS2017, derived from S4] Construction-pose geometry for Stan: hip 2.99 m, knee 1.94 m (0.29 m ahead of hip), ankle 0.89 m, MTP 0.29 m. Thigh 15.6 deg from vertical (knee forward), shank 17.4 deg back, metatarsus 12.2 deg back (MTP behind ankle), digit III extending 0.58 m forward. Shoulder 2.50 m, snout 2.05 m, tail tip 3.0 m. COM sits 0.66 m ahead of the hip, in front of the toes, so this is a modelling pose, not a balanced standing posture.

[H2011 Table 3 vs museum figures] H2011 'leg length' (3.04-3.30 m) is a summed limb length, not standing hip height. The Field Museum's '13 ft tall at the hip' for SUE (3.96 m) is to the top of the hips; the ilium rises ~0.64 m above the acetabulum (SIMM2017 MOR 555, derived). For a robot hip-pitch axis use acetabulum height, plausibly ~2.45-3.1 m for a SUE/Stan-sized adult.

[FMNH2017, FMNH2018B] SUE 2018 remount: Makovicky says T. rex 'had a bulging belly' and the stance was changed to 'walking rather than skulking'. Gastralia were added (26 of ~60; first pair 44 in / 1.12 m apart at the tips), the ribs widened, the furcula corrected, the shoulder blades adjusted, and the arms lowered and brought forward until they could touch. [WIKI_SUE] With the correct furcula the shoulders meet near the chest midline.

[H2011] Torso shape: SUE's and Carnegie's 2000-era mounts have proportionately longer, wider and taller torsos ('barrel-chested', from dorsally displaced transverse processes). Fig. 7 readings: chest width 1.05-1.65 m, chest height 1.40-1.68 m, inter-glenoid 0.49-0.77 m, 'sacral height' ~2.0-2.1 m. No complete gastral basket was available, so ventral torso contours were approximated.

[H2011 Tables 6-7] Whole-body COM lies 0.38-0.80 m in front of and 0.33-0.52 m below the hip joint (12-27% and 10-17% of leg length). The body is front-heavy about the hip, balanced by a heavy tail (10-21% of mass) and large hip extensors.

[WR2009, STEVENSWEB] Alert head posture was depressed below horizontal; Stevens summarises labyrinth and vision evidence as a habitual head pitch of about 5-10 deg nose-down. [SN2006 / Stevens 2006] Binocular field ~55 deg, so the eyes face forward over a narrow snout. [HS2003] In dorsal view the T. rex skull is extremely broad posteriorly and narrows towards the snout, more so than Tarbosaurus; laterally the skull is deep (~0.41 depth/length).

[PADIAN2022] On the UCMP MOR 555-based mount the neck is S-shaped: anterior horizontal section 45 cm, middle diagonal 75 cm, posterior horizontal 60 cm. The skull tip is only 135 cm in front of the glenoid, so the head is carried close to the shoulders. [SR2007] M. transversospinalis capitis probably filled the posterior dorsal concavity of the neck, giving a smoother, crocodilian-like dorsal neck profile. Adult T. rex had relatively large head-dorsiflexor attachment areas.

[PC2011] The M. caudofemoralis was exceptionally large, enlarged in Tyrannosaurus by dorsoventrally lengthened hemal arches, so the tail base is deep and muscular. [H2011 Table 8] CFL 2.0-3.9% of body mass per side. [VB2021] Model tail is passively supported by ligaments, with natural frequency ~0.66 Hz matching step frequency. [SELLERS2017 derived] The modelled tail tip is near hip height, i.e. the tail is held roughly horizontal.

[PADIAN2022] Forelimbs are tiny: humerus 37 cm (0.285 femur), ulna 20 cm, digits I/II 22/25 cm. They cannot reach in front of the head. Glenoids ~68 cm apart on the mount; MOR 555 lacks a furcula, so the coracoids may sit too close together. [H2011 Table 5] One forelimb is 0.1-0.4% of body mass.
gauge_and_gait_findings: [MCCREA2014] Bellatoripes fredlundi Trackway A (tyrannosaurid, Wapiti Fm., not T. rex): mean FL 57.9 cm, FW 51.9 cm, paces 174 and 173 cm, stride 346 cm. The diagnosis reads: 'Footprints in trackway are in line, with a pace angulation nearing 180 deg. Trackway width is narrow, with footprints overlapping the midline of the trackway. Footprint rotation is slight, but generally toward the trackway midline.' Table 1 prints PA = 117 deg, which contradicts its own paces and stride (they give 171 deg).

[MCCREA2014, derived] Recomputed pace angulation is 171 deg (166-180 deg allowing +/-0.5 cm rounding). The left-right print centrelines are ~13 cm apart (0-21 cm), about 0.23 footprint lengths or ~0.05 of hip height, so the feet land almost on the midline.

[MCCREA2014] Trackmaker hip height 2.87 m (straight leg; 2.80 m with the general large-theropod equation) or 2.30 m (knee 110 deg, ankle 140 deg). Walking speed 6.4-8.5 km/h (1.8-2.4 m/s). Relative stride 3.46 m / h = 1.21-1.50 (derived); the paper's stated 1.69 does not follow from its numbers. Rotations: +6, -9 (outward; pathology compensation) and +5 deg in A; +12 and +20 deg in C. Trackway C pace 155 cm.

[SCINEWS2026 reporting Falkingham et al. 2026, JVP] First trackway attributed to an adult T. rex (Hell Creek Fm., North Dakota): 4 prints over ~7 m, each ~1 m long, stride ~4 m, walking ~1.5-2 m/s, narrow angle between toe impressions. Pace angulation and trackway width were not obtainable because the paper was blocked; this is the most important missing gauge source.

[SD2016 reporting Smith, Persons & Xing 2016] Glenrock trackway (Lance Fm., Wyoming): three sequential tracks of a subadult T. rex or Nanotyrannus; walking speed 4.5-8 km/h. No gauge numbers obtained.

[WIKI_TPUS, MCCREA2014] The single Tyrannosauripus pillmorei print is 86 x 64 cm, ~40% longer and ~20% wider than Bellatoripes. Adult T. rex tracks are ~0.86-1.0 m long and include a broad metatarsal pad impression.

[VB2021] Trix tail-resonance model: preferred walking speed 1.28 m/s (0.80-1.64), step frequency ~0.66 Hz, 1.94 m steps at 3.1 m hip height (relative stride ~1.25). Literature trackway-based large-theropod walking speeds are 2-3 m/s. [SELLERS2017] Stress limits confine T. rex to walking/grounded running. [FMNH2018B] SUE top speed is a 'fast walk' of 15 mph (6.7 m/s). [H2011] Literature top speeds 5-11 m/s.

[H2005] The MOR 555 model reaches narrow-gauge foot placement through 10 deg hip abduction plus 15 deg tibiotarsal valgus (knees out, feet in), explicitly to match theropod footprints. [SELLERS2017, derived] The sagittal-only multibody model places the feet 0.92 m apart against 0.69 m hip spacing (ratio 1.33), so copying such a model gives a wide gauge no trackway shows.

[Derived design gauge, interpretive] Walking trackways imply each foot lands ~0.2-0.3 m medial to its own hip joint in a Stan-sized animal: foot spacing ~0.05 h against hip spacing ~0.23 h. Stance-phase limb adduction or knee valgus of roughly 5-10 deg is needed. No trackway data constrain the static standing gauge, which may be wider.
[Dimensionless walking range, derived] Froude number v^2/(g h) ~0.05-0.25, relative stride ~1.2-1.5, pace/FL ~2 (adult T. rex) to 3 (Bellatoripes).
open_questions: Brochu 2003 (SUE osteology memoir) is closed access and was not read. SUE's MT III, pedal digit, ilium, scapula and humerus lengths remain unverified. Only the tibia (1143 mm) is confirmed through an open secondary source (LONGRICH2026). Blog values measured off Brochu's figures (femur 132-143 cm, humerus 39 cm, dentary 101 cm) conflict and were not used.

SUE femur 1321 mm and circumference 579/580 mm come only from secondary sources (blogs and an unattributed DECECCHI2020 row). H2011 gives 1.312 m from scans. SUE skull length 1.394 m appears only in Wikipedia with a weak citation.

Scotty (RSM P2523.8) femur ~133 cm and circumference ~590 mm (Persons et al. 2020) are unverified: the Wiley full text was blocked by a bot challenge, and only the abstract, a ScienceDaily release (>8,800 kg, ~13 m) and Wikipedia (8,870 kg) were read.

Standing acetabulum height for adult T. rex is not stated in any accessible primary source. The 2.44-3.2 m range is derived from model files (SELLERS2017 2.99 m construction pose; SIMM 3.225 m fully columnar), VB2021's 3.1 m simulation input, and 0.80-0.95 x limb length. The full texts of Hutchinson & Garcia 2002 and Gatesy et al. 2009 would tighten it.

H2011 internal inconsistencies found by arithmetic, not addressed by the 2014 correction: (a) each Table 6 total equals the Table 4 axial segments plus ONE forelimb and ONE hindlimb from Table 5 (Stan min 4374 + 1560 = 5934; MOR min 5777 exact), yet Table 10 doubles per-limb masses. If limbs are per side, totals omit the contralateral limbs; corrected minimal totals would be Carnegie ~8905, SUE ~11330, Stan ~7494, MOR ~7258 kg (Stan's ~7.5 t matches SELLERS2017's 7.2 t). (b) Carnegie 'average mass' 9081 kg should be (7394+14564)/2 = 10979. (c) Table 8 Stan maximal CFL '22 kg' should be ~423 kg (3.90% of 10837). (d) SUE's maximal segment sum is 18329 vs 18489 in the table. Use mass fractions with caution.

McCrea 2014 internal inconsistencies: Table 1 pace angulation 117 deg against 171 deg from its own paces and stride and 'nearing 180 deg' in the diagnosis; stated stride/h of 1.69 against 1.21-1.50 from its stride and h values. The 2015 correction covers only a duplicated reference.

Falkingham et al. 2026 (JVP) adult T. rex trackway: pace angulation, trackway width, rotation and exact print and stride lengths are still needed. Only press-rounded values (1 m prints, 4 m stride, 1.5-2 m/s) were obtained; tandfonline returned a 403 challenge.

Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1): femur 788 mm (reconstructed on the cast, H2011) vs 720 mm (other studies; PC2016). Its taxonomy is disputed (LONGRICH2026 calls it the holotype of 'Nanotyrannus' lethaeus), so the 'juvenile T. rex' proportions in H2011 may not be T. rex. LACM 23845 is a juvenile alternative (tibia equal to femur).
Source typos and ambiguities: SNIVELY2006 lists 'BHI 2033 (TMP 98.86.1)' (140 cm skull), possibly meaning BHI 3033 (Stan). HS2003 Table 1 caption says 'BHI-3038' while its rows say BHI-3033.

H2011 Fig. 7 values (chest width/height, inter-glenoid distance, sacral length/height) are read from a chart (+/-0.05 m), not tabulated; my GAD read-back matched Table 3 within 0.01 m. Interpreting 'sacral height' as pelvic depth (ilium top to pubic boot) is my inference.

Chest width is uncertain (1.05-1.65 m): H2011 calls the 2000-era SUE and Carnegie ribcages artefactually wide, yet the 2018 SUE remount widened the ribs to fit the gastralia. The 2018 remount's dimensions were not published in accessible sources.

Joint-centre segment lengths differ by ~10% between published models of similar-sized animals (thigh 1.09 m in SELLERS2017 Stan vs 1.22 m in the MOR 555 SIMM model, femora both ~1.28 m), because of joint-centre placement and soft-tissue allowances. The SIMM bone meshes are ~6-9% longer than caliper lengths, so only their ratios were used.

Neck length rests on one approximate mount measurement (PADIAN2022); cervical centrum lengths (Brochu 2003) were not accessible. The 5-10 deg head-down figure comes from the author's web summary of a Science discussion, not from a table.

Design-template cautions (interpretive, for the parent workflow): designlab/template.py states 'hip height is ~25-27% of body length (Hutchinson et al. 2011, table 3)', but that column is summed limb length; standing acetabulum height is ~0.21-0.25 of body length. Anatomical neck (cervical column ~1.5 skull lengths), pubic boot depth (~0.5 H below the acetabulum) and walking foot gauge (~0.2 x hip spacing) differ markedly from the template's current values.
